svg.text: The git write-roots guard: which git metadata the fence re-opens
reckon._backends.worktree_git_write_roots(worktree) feeds fence_argv's writable roots
Linked worktree (a dispatched run)
git dir = Code/.reckon-worktrees/<pool>/<node>/.git/worktrees/x
common = Code/<checkout>/.git
git dir != common → helper grants:
grants[0] = worktree's own .git dir (HEAD, index, reflog)
grants[1] = common .git/objects (append-only store)
fence_argv writable binds then name both, so a commit lands
while refs/heads, the index and the main tree stay sealed.
Pinned by test_a_fenced_worker_commits_in_its_own_worktree
and its negative control (grant removed → read-only refusal).
Main checkout as the worktree (the pinned case)
git dir = Code/<checkout>/.git
common = Code/<checkout>/.git (the same path)
git dir == common → early return, helper grants:
grants = [] — nothing named
so .git and .git/objects are not writable binds
refs/heads, the index and the working tree of a main checkout
are exactly what the fence seals, so none may be re-opened.
Pinned by test_a_main_checkout_worktree_grants_no_git_roots;
its control deletes the early return and the case fails there.
Declaration: deleting the early return names the main checkout's .git dir and .git/objects among the writable binds, and the new case fails.
